name: Thiel Fellowship
stage: Idea-stage: yes (pre-team, pre-company accepted). FAQ: 'You don't need to have incorporated a company or built a full product yet' and 'we review and accept applicants as individuals'. Must be aged 22 or younger and without a university degree; fellows skip or stop out of college.
check_size_terms: $250,000 grant spread over two years; no equity ('We do not take equity in your company').
geography: Global (no geographic restriction stated in the FAQ); age 22 or younger.
application_timing: rolling ('we accept applications year round'). No deadline.
best_channel: application form (rolling). A general team email exists, but the site directs applicants to the form.
notes: Looks for young people who 'want to build new things' and 'take on big risks' instead of following a traditional track. Applicants are judged as individuals, so no cofounder or company is needed. Grant was raised to $250K from the class of 2026 (third-party reports).

name: 776 Foundation Fellowship (776 Fellowship)
stage: Idea-stage: yes (projects, not companies; pre-company accepted). Official text: two-year, full-time program for 18-24 year olds 'to work on projects to fight climate change instead of pursuing a university degree'.
check_size_terms: $100,000 grant over two years, paid quarterly; no equity (grant).
sectors: Climate change (2025 review page also mentions 'Climate and Frontier Innovation').
geography: Global ('Fellows must be ages 18 to 24 and can live anywhere in the world'; final remote interview).
application_url: https://www.776.org/ (application form appears on the site when a cycle is open; email signup for notification otherwise)
application_timing: batch. Program still runs. Site text (from the site JS bundle): 'Check back later this year for our 2026 Application' and 'Our 5th Cohort will be selected May 2026, with a start date of June 2026'. Past windows opened late March and closed mid April (2025 deadline: April 14). Current open/closed status for the 2026 window: unknown (site is JS-rendered; text may be stale).
best_channel: application form (when the cycle is open); sign up on the site for the opening notice. No cold-email address published.
notes: Inspired by the Thiel Fellowship; ~20 fellows per cohort; fellows leave or skip university to work full time on a climate project. Funded by Alexis Ohanian's 776 Foundation ($20M commitment). Site lists a '2025 776 Fellowship Year in Review', so the program was active in 2025.

name: Soma Capital (Soma Fellows / direct)
stage: Idea-stage: yes for Soma Fellows (official site: 'check out our fellows program if you're just getting started'; third-party listings: open to anyone building early-stage companies, skews to founders in early-to-mid 20s and students). Direct fund invests pre-seed/seed.
check_size_terms: Official fellows page: 'Track 1: Up to $2m uncapped for your startup' with 'potential fast 10m+ follow on funding for strong traction'. Instrument and equity not stated on the official page. Third-party listings report a typical $100K uncapped SAFE.
sectors: Generalist; AI/ML and data infrastructure prominent in portfolio (OpenAI, Anthropic, Databricks listed).
geography: Global; office space in SF and NY (third-party: also Boston; remote participation with optional in-person events).
application_timing: unknown. Third-party listings conflict: one lists Spring and Fall cohorts (Spring 2026 deadline April 1, 2026; Fall programming Oct 10 to Nov 17), another calls it 'a rolling fellowship'. The official page shows no deadline.
best_channel: application form; cold outreach accepted (Soma's X post invites past applicants to 'shoot us a note with updates').
notes: Looks for 'brilliant superhumans pushing humanity forward'; claims 40+ unicorns seeded. Track 2 of the fellows program places engineers into portfolio companies. Weekly dinners and events with unicorn founders are part of the program (third-party).

name: LAUNCH / Founder University (Jason Calacanis)
stage: Idea-stage: yes ('12-week pre-accelerator for 0-to-1'; built for founders in 'Year Zero' and Year One; idea, MVP, or existing product all accepted).
check_size_terms: Official: '$25K or $125K' invested into top graduates; instrument and equity not stated on the site. Third-party: $125K for 7% on a post-money SAFE, optional follow-on up to $375K on an uncapped MFN SAFE. Tuition $500, refundable if you join every live session.
geography: Virtual (global) with optional in-person components; LAUNCH is based in the US.
application_timing: rolling ('You can apply to Founder University at any time... Upon acceptance, founders will be assigned to the next cohort'). Site text lists 'Cohort 13 — Early 2026'; a third-party list says Cohort 13 is Fall 2026. Exact next cohort start: unknown.
best_channel: application form; cold email possible (founderu@launch.co is in the official site code).
notes: 'We invest in founders who show up, ship fast, and never stop building.' Two live virtual sessions per week; investment goes only to top graduates. LAUNCH Accelerator ($125K, 14 weeks) is the later-stage sibling program.

name: On Deck Founders (ODF)
stage: Idea-stage: yes (pre-company, pre-team). Admissions page: ideal candidates are '100% committed (or soon committing) to starting a company'; not suitable if you 'already raised beyond pre-seed' or 'already have a team'.
check_size_terms: No investment. Non-dilutive ('We don't take any equity'). Pay-what-you-can fee, suggested $1000 USD. $800k+ in perks (AWS, Stripe, Mercury, Carta).
geography: Global applicants; one-week in-person program in San Francisco; then online community.
application_timing: batch. joinodf.com says next cohort ODF28 launches Q1 2027; admissions.joinodf.com says 'ODF28 kicks off in Q3 2026' (conflict; the main site is likely newer). No deadline published. Process: apply, optional video, interview, decision in ~36 hours.
best_channel: application form. Admissions page also lists founders@joinodf.com.
notes: beondeck.com now redirects to joinodf.com; ODF is a one-week SF program plus a 3,000+ member community, not an investor. Screens for 'exceptional builder talent and unfair advantages' and 'trajectory over resume'. Claims 1,000+ startups launched and $2B+ raised by alumni.

name: Conviction Embed (Sarah Guo)
stage: Idea-stage: yes (pre-company, solo founders accepted). Official FAQ: 'I just got started/haven't incorporated/don't have a cofounder. Am I too early to apply? No!'
check_size_terms: $250K on an uncapped, no-discount MFN SAFE (or at the price of a round closed within the last 60 days). Plus $350K AWS credits, $350K Azure credits, and $500K+ other compute/inference/hosting credits.
geography: Global applicants; mandatory in-person retreat in San Francisco.
application_timing: batch (about twice a year). Program still runs. Official page: 'Apply early to the 7th cohort', 'Applications are now open', 'Rolling admissions over the month'; retreat September 11-13 and demo day November 12 (no year shown). A third-party listing gives an August 10, 2026 deadline for this cohort, which has passed. Status for cohort 7: likely closed; next cohort date unknown.
notes: Eight-week program for AI-native founding teams; some cohort members have already raised. Focus is community, fundraising and hiring workshops, and compute. Founded by Sarah Guo (partner Mike Vernal).

name: AI Grant (Nat Friedman / Daniel Gross)
stage: Idea-stage: partly. Targets 'pre-seed/seed-stage startups'; 'no credentials required'; single founders accepted; must be or become a Delaware corporation. 'Demos are a big plus', so a working prototype helps.
check_size_terms: $250,000 on an uncapped SAFE ('no cap, no discount MFN SAFE') plus $350,000 in Azure credits and $250,000 in additional credits.
application_url: unknown (no open form; 'Applications for Batch 4 are closed')
application_timing: batch. Batch 4 closed (applications were due August 9, 2024). No Batch 5 announced as of 2026-09-02; status unknown.
best_channel: application form when a batch opens; follow @aigrant for the announcement. No cold-pitch route published.
notes: Looks for 'technical & pragmatic founders who want to build great products' and 'smart and energetic people with actionable ideas that are clearly useful'. Backed Perplexity and others. Note: aigrant.org is the older open-source grant; aigrant.com is the equity program.

name: Betaworks Camp
stage: Idea-stage: possible but a demo is encouraged. FAQ: a product is 'not required, but having something to show like a demo or beta or Figma is highly encouraged'. Early-stage companies, typically 8-12 per cohort.
check_size_terms: Up to $500K per team: 'Betaworks and our syndicate partners will each invest up to $250k'. Spring 2026 terms post: Betaworks Ventures up to $250K on an uncapped SAFE with a 25% discount plus a 5% common stock stake; syndicate up to $250K on uncapped SAFEs with the same discount. No program fee.
sectors: AI; theme changes per camp (current: 'AI Camp: The New Agent Economy'; Spring 2026: Agent Systems).
geography: Global applicants; in person in New York (Meatpacking District) for the first and final two weeks; 12-week program.
application_timing: batch. Site banner: 'Application now open for AI Camp: The New Agent Economy' with 'Deadline Extended'; no date published. Fall sessions run August to November; spring sessions March to May (applications Dec-Jan).
email: unknown (site lists only eventsny@betaworks.com for event inquiries)
best_channel: application form. No program email or cold-pitch route published.
notes: Thematic camps; the Spring 2026 camp wanted companies 'newly designed assuming agentic AI as a core tenet' and complete, autonomous solutions. Founders pay their own travel and housing in NYC.

name: 500 Global (Flagship Accelerator)
stage: Idea-stage: no. Official portal: 'early-stage tech startups'; third-party guides say seed-stage with some traction. A company must exist to take the investment.
check_size_terms: $150,000 investment for a 6% stake, 'subject to terms and diligence' (official). Third-party: $37,500 program fee deducted from the investment.
geography: Global founders; four-month in-person program in Silicon Valley (Palo Alto / San Francisco).
application_timing: rolling applications ('apply any time of year'). Portal shows Batch 37 open (third-party: Batch 37 starts Q2 2026). The 500.co page still shows stale Batch 36 text (deadline October 11). Current batch number and next deadline: unknown.
email: unknown (site lists only partnerships@500.co and press@500.co)
best_channel: application form. No founder-facing email published.
notes: 30-40 companies per batch; $1M+ in credits via 500 FounderHub. Acceptance rate estimated near 3% (third-party). Many regional programs (LatAm, MENA, Eurasia, Japan, Korea) exist with different terms.

name: Plug and Play Tech Center
stage: Idea-stage: no. Vertical accelerators favor startups that can pilot with corporate partners (pre-seed to growth). Third-party guides say idea-stage teams without traction fit poorly.
check_size_terms: Accelerator seat is equity-free with no program fee (third-party sources). Plug and Play Ventures invests separately via SAFE or convertible note; reported checks $25K-$500K (third-party). Official pages are JS-rendered and no terms could be read from them.
sectors: 20+ verticals: fintech, insurtech, health, supply chain, energy, mobility, real estate, food, AI, and more.
application_timing: batch per vertical (about two batches per year, ~12 weeks); applications accepted year round; deadlines vary by vertical and location. Next deadline: unknown.
best_channel: application form (per-program form on the site). No email or cold-pitch route verified.
notes: Corporate-innovation platform; value is corporate pilots and business development, not a guaranteed check. Was the most active accelerator worldwide 2020-2022 (Wikipedia). Acceptance rate about 5% (third-party).
